nap-18070209-375: I send you a line, my Friend, lest you be uneasy. Enemy lost the battle, 40 guns, 12 standards, 12,000 prisoners; he suffered horridly. I lost 1,600 killed and between 3,000 and 4,000 wounded.
nap-18070220-376: I see conscription goes well. Sanguinary affair at Eylau on the eighth; my right at Ostralenka on the sixteenth -- Russians beaten both. No importance to Kosciusco -- not esteemed in his country, his conduct proves him a fool.
nap-18070310-381: I see Paris gossips more of Mlle Aubry than of all the army losses; Lugay wronged her by coldness. She who played Goddess of Reason now plays Glory, and fell breaking her arm before the Empress.
nap-18070401-382: I am delighted to hear nothing more of Madame de Stael -- when I trouble myself about her it is when I have facts before me. That woman is a regular crow; she thought she saw the tempest coming. Let her go to Her Lake Leman.
nap-18070404-383: My Son -- send Lauriston 25 watches for Turks, 25 to Marmont. You claim 20,000 men with grand army -- you dont believe it; you have 10,000, and what men! Make soldiers, not marshals, knights, counts. You govern Holland like a Capucin -- a king orders, asks nothing.
nap-18070414-384: Displeased with your preamble suppressing monasteries. In religion use language of religion, not philosophy -- the art of governing. Why speak of monks services to art and science? Your preamble philosophical, insults the evicted.
nap-18070502-386: My Friend -- I see with pleasure you are in good health and always fond of Malmaison. It is said the arch-chancellor has fallen in love -- is this a joke, or true? It greatly amuses me.
nap-18070601-387: Hope the week-finished campaign pleases my people. Russian army more crushed than ever the Austrians -- Beningsen showed little talent. Their soldiers good but weakened, discouraged. My army superb, unscathed. Conscription goes well.
nap-18070602-388: I have just seen the Emperor of Russia in the middle of the Niemen on a raft with a handsome flag. Tomorrow the Emperor presents the king of Prussia to me and comes to reside here -- I have neutralised Tilsit. I wish you to arrive as speedily as possible.
nap-18070615-389: My Friend -- few words, very tired, bivouacking days. My children celebrated Marengo anniversary. Friedland as glorious -- Russian army routed, 80 guns, 30,000 taken or killed, 25 generals; guard annihilated -- sister of Marengo, Austerlitz, Jena. My loss small.
nap-18070622-390: While St. Denis unready, place the little Napoleon's body in Notre Dame chapel. Proclamation: Frenchmen, worthy of yourselves and me -- return with laurels after glorious, durable peace. Time for country to live in repose from England. My recompenses prove my gratitude and love.
nap-18070701-391: My Friend -- queen of Prussia dined with me. I defended against further concessions to her husband; galant but adhered to policy. She is very amiable. When you read this, peace concluded with Russia and Prussia, Jerome king of Westphalia.
nap-18070701-392: The queen of Prussia is really charming; she is full of coquetterie towards me. But do not be jealous -- I am an oilcloth off which all that runs. It would cost me too dear to play the galant.
nap-18070701-393: Guilleminot to Michelson HQ, then Grand Vizir -- inform peace concluded, treaty articles for Porte. Then Constantinople with cipher to Sebastiani -- tell my ambassador my system on Porte shaky, changing; not decided; greatest friendship with Russia.
nap-18070706-395: I see with pain you are an egotist -- the success of my arms has no attraction for you. The handsome queen of Prussia comes to dine with me today. I am in good health and greatly wish to see you when destiny permits -- probability not long.
nap-18070714-396: Sir my Brother -- to express viva voce the sentiments you inspire, I send my aide-de-camp Savary, appointed ambassador to your court. Receive him with your peculiar kindness.
nap-18070722-397: I have asked Alquier to insist on the number of French cardinals. The Russians plunder and burn villages and massacre the poor and rich; Austerlitz broke their prestige.
nap-18070922-401: Lima saw Murat without presentation -- duty as my brother-in-law, grand admiral, reigning prince. My displeasure. Metternich presented properly. With Segur, report on ambassador reception. All settled before Friday for Russian ambassador.
nap-18070925-402: I send for Izquierdo on Spain debt, Portugal, Etruria. Portugal: I see no difficulty giving Spain suzerainty, portion for Etruria queen and prince of peace. Etruria: difficult Spanish branch in Italy now all Italy mine.
nap-18071007-403: Courier to Junot: enter Spain in 24 hours, march Portugal. Ambassador left Lisbon -- no moment to lose. To Charles IV: Holland, confederation, you, Alexander, I unite to drive English, avenge Denmark -- Portugal last resistance.
nap-18071014-404: I send for province descriptions, roads, ground. Sketches by engineers -- village distances, nature, resources. I do not leave my army -- a general never leaves it; great only with it, small at court. Portugal war on England not enough -- I march on.
nap-18071101-405: Marescalchi sends me Spain treaty -- Tuscany mine, I unite to Italy. Leghorn troops suffice, I prepare secretly. Lucca coins: Napoleon protege l Italia not suitable; replacing Dieu protege la France indecent.
nap-18071201-406: I saw Lucien at Mantua -- he promised daughter to Paris by winter. Lucien conflicted, lacked decision. I urged him to serve me and country. Daughter must start with declaration at my disposal. No moment lost. Events march. I await answer on Charlotte.
nap-18080107-407: My Brother -- Brunswick petition. No reply -- he omitted subject in letter, you recognise only subjects. Brunswick prince presence damaging, not permitted. In 2-3 years retirement ok. Meanwhile no reply.
nap-18080301-413: I published the four-million contribution before mastering the country. Since entering Portugal you did nothing I desired. The Portuguese troops should have marched for France long since, reaching Bayonne for me to organise. You left the forts months in Portuguese hands.
nap-18080302-414: My Son -- Cardinal Ruffo (Calabrias) to Paris, Cardinal Ruffo Scylla (Naples archbishop) to Bologna, two dangerous cardinals removed. Miollis: no arrangement with Rome; orders contempt, seize temporal government. Battalions through Vatican. Allow Lent before settling Rome.
nap-18080310-415: Approve Miollis -- treat Roman soldiers well, dismiss bad officers. Send Neapolitan and my cardinals from Rome: Litta to Milan, Genoese to Genoa, Italians to Italy, Piedmontese to Piedmont, Neapolitans to Naples. Caraffa responsible for stone from window.
nap-18080316-416: Ordered Neapolitan cardinals at Rome sent to you for allegiance. You sent them to Alessandria -- I cannot understand. What fear from 2-3 old priests? Oath excellent effect. Pope calls you Prince Joseph, makes your cardinals refuse oath. If you fear 2-3 old men, throne insecure.
nap-18080401-417: Received your letter with queen, Charlotte, Zenaide. At Bayonne. Infant Don Carlos ill. Expect Ferdinand VII on frontier, King Charles and queen. To Ferdinand: father papers show my interest in your family.
nap-18080401-418: I see ambassador language in Paris -- hardly believe Tolstoy used attributed words, a quolibet. My Reply: couriers brought Moldavia rupture, Finland conquest, fresh troops. Courts on best terms. My quarrels Rome/Spain nothing to do with Russia. Good terms with all.
nap-18080501-419: Spanish ambassador complains papers say Charles forced abdication. I tell him: I saw king and queen receive son badly; under poinard hours, would perish if refused. Prince Asturias stupid, bad-hearted, enemy of France. I arrested couriers -- letters hate French.
nap-18080501-420: I say confidentially: Charles gets Compiegne for life, Chambord, forest, 30M real pension. He cedes Spanish throne. Charles excellent. Starts tomorrow, week Fontainebleau. Asturias no interest -- so stupid no word drawn. Madrid and Burgos lesson decides.
nap-18080503-422: I refused the Prince of Asturias’s request to see me as Majesty, but received him as Royal Highness.
nap-18080601-423: King of Naples arrived, acknowledged Spain king, leaving for Madrid. Oath from grandees, Castille, India, Inquisition. Dupont 15k at Seville, Saragossa revolted. King arrival ends disturbances. English king death -- great joy to me.
nap-18080802-425: I have sent you Villoutreys’s examination of the Dupont affair. Vedel and Gobert were not involved, and they capitulated to save their baggage. Such cowardice shames the French name.
nap-18080810-426: I have received an extraordinary courier from Caulaincourt: Alexander says he will help if Austria makes war, and he is concerned about Spain.
nap-18080910-427: Marescot signed infamous capitulation -- I deprived employment. Madame Marescot cannot remain lady in waiting. Crime: not responsible for Baylen but sanctioned capitulation. Paid dearly for generosity.
nap-18080910-428: Caulaincourt: Alexander leaves Erfurth twelfth. I send Lannes to Vistula to meet you. To Soult: papers on Stein letter. I demanded dismissal from Ministry or Prussia king not return. I sequestered Westphalia property. Austria far from war. I am sure of Russia.
nap-18080914-429: Madam my Sister -- delighted your Berlin return, my dearest wish. King and you resume former sentiments. To Spain king at Miranda: no reply to bad temper -- principle. Too much intelligence not to understand this only response.
nap-18081001-430: My Friend -- well. Shooting Jena field -- breakfasted where bivouacked. Weimar ball: Alexander danced, not I; forty years forty years. Health good despite ailing. Erfurth convention: Finland, Moldavia, Wallachia Russian = peace with England condition.
nap-18081014-431: Concluded all with Alexander. Start tomorrow Paris, Bayonne within month. Send exact army report. War closable by single manoeuvre, I must be there. Reduced Prussia contribution 20M; told Austria never supposed hostilities resume.
nap-18081101-432: I just arrived. Troops scattered -- write me twice daily for corps positions. I rode Landes at gallop, tired. Fourth: Tolosa, Vittoria next night, orders to Moncey, Ney, Berthier. Spanish defeats: Castanos Logrono, Blake Durango, Burgos. Eleventh I entered Burgos.
nap-18081126-433: Tudela matches Espinosa. Andalusia under Castanos, Aragon under Palafox, Valentia and new Castile, all broken and scattered; guns, baggage and prisoners taken. Then Somo-Sierra: my Polish lancers carried the battery.
nap-18070804-398: I do not know what rash act you suppose the Pope capable of. You should have sent troops toward Bologna -- if he commits an imprudence, a fine opportunity to deprive him of the Roman states. I wrote the king of Wurtemberg for Princess Catherine for my Brother Jerome.
nap-18070810-399: I am proprietor in Warsaw of all debts due to the king of Prussia by private individuals -- money advanced on land security, 60M francs. War requisitions: Germany 24.2M, Italy 1.2M, Spain 2.88M, Portugal 0.64M, Austria 2M arrears. Total 30.92M.
nap-18080217-412: Whence come journal details on Caulaincourt? The Publiciste should not praise Lambert. I order articles describing him as a traitor who fought against his country. Savary coldly received in Russia -- nobility houses closed.
nap-18090301-439: I hasten to inform you I have deemed fit to create your Son Prince Napoleon Louis Grand Duke of Berg. You were vexed at this creation without consulting you. Saragossa fell after heroic resistance. A stain on Lannes: he violated capitulation, executed two gallant defenders.
nap-18090321-440: I received your letter. War appears imminent. Best thing: assemble troops to defend your country and serve the common cause. First time you ask my advice.
nap-18090501-441: My Friend -- I received your letter. The bullet which touched me did not wound me -- barely shaved the Achilles tendon. My health very good; you are wrong to feel uneasy. My affairs go well.
nap-18090519-442: You greatly alarmed Paris about Prussia. Even if she attacked us, Prussia is of no consequence, easily subdued. You have not shown sufficient prudence -- bad effect when a power thinks I am not in position to fight. In ninth bulletin: throwing bridge across Danube.
nap-18090601-443: I reply to your letter on Carnot. If he merely helped relieve Manberige he would have my gratitude. As War minister he has right to a pension. I make no difficulty employing him as he wishes. Let me know his embarrassments. Carnot, entirely ruined, applied for army employment.
nap-18090701-444: I send a page with good news: victory at Enzersdorf and Wagram. Enemy army flying in disorder. Everything goes according to my wishes. Eugene well. Aldobrandini slightly wounded; Bessieres thigh grazed. Lasalle killed.
nap-18090701-445: I see the bull of excommunication is so ridiculous it does not deserve attention. What deserves attention: provide for vacant sees. Must know what Pope intends -- if he does not confirm bishops per Concordat he will create a schism.
nap-18090710-446: You know my intentions on a Tyrol expedition. Be at Innsbruck by summer. No ridiculous proclamations; be severe; disarm the country; take many hostages and make examples. Act with celerity.
nap-18090722-447: Prince Liechtenstein handed me your Majesty's letter, in which you inform me that you have appointed negotiators to treat for peace.
nap-18090801-448: What a lost hour! Thirty thousand English, far from the sea, facing a hundred thousand of the world's best troops! Had Soult joined, one blow could have ended it. I blame hesitation, and I will have energy.
nap-18090801-449: It is repugnant to my feelings to suppose Flushing surrendered -- that appears impossible. Such conduct would be cowardice approaching treason. Flushing can defend itself as long as it has a morsel of bread. Enemy cannot have destroyed inundation means.
nap-18090901-450: You have no confidence in Abbe de Pradt. I do not know if I told you to distrust that man as greatest enemy we can have. Profound hypocrite, neither morality nor talent of his condition, addicted to intrigue leading to scaffold. Treat him as usual, let this remain secret.
nap-18090904-451: I saw in Moniteur details you inserted on Spain; they are not sufficient. This does not compensate for immense English relations. Publish letters of different generals, effacing what is for government only. Letters from Soult, Moncey, Sebastiani should be published.
nap-18091007-452: I write to king of Spain: English reports claim they took guns, state number; all army letters certify this; Senarmont says six guns taken. Find how many lost at Talavera -- slightest omission criminal; not for publication, to know truth.
nap-18091010-453: Reports this morning show enemy retreating as fast as he can. Battlefield covered with dead. I am about to get on horseback to examine situation, attack if he occupies positions, pursue if falling back. To king of Saxony: I wrote from battlefield.
nap-18091021-454: I arrived here yesterday in good health. Stop a day at Stuttgart. You shall receive 24 hours notice of my arrival at Fontainebleau. Great pleasure to see you again, await with impatience. I embrace you.
nap-18091028-455: I beg you write an historical sketch proving: popes always enemies of power predominating in Italy. When Germans triumphed they called the French; when French masters they leagued with Germans to drive them out.
nap-18091121-456: Tell Spain's king: had Ney stayed at Salamanca, my army had suffered no such affront. Marchand cannot command in chief. When I send marshals I feel the need; no method rules this Spanish campaign. Del Parque's Spaniards beat us and hold Salamanca, answer it.
nap-18091122-457: I see with pleasure you arrived at Milan. You wrote a work on your Italian campaign -- send it to me. My financial affairs here in great disorder. English expedition cost 2M. New levies and immense armaments for Spain continue to ruin me.
nap-18091201-458: My brother, Roumanzoff's second note grieves me. Why reopen what my Vienna letter settled? I declared before Europe my will on Warsaw, Moldavia, Wallachia. What more is asked? I cannot slay chimeras and fight clouds. Judge whose language fits alliance: yours or mine.
nap-18100106-459: I write to Rome for the fisherman ring, the seals of the pontiff, the ornaments of the tiara, everything used by the Pope in ceremonies. At seizure of Pope papers a packet of golden pieces found in Doria portfolio, returned without remark that the fisherman ring was among them.
nap-18100127-460: Write Laforest at Madrid: present notes on impossibility of meeting Spain enormous expenses; I already sent 300M francs there; such sums exhaust France. Add war with Austria cost much. Much money in provinces.
nap-18100206-461: Send a courier to Caulaincourt tonight. The council splits between a Russian and an Austrian match, and France over religion. As for the Princess Anne talk, girls ripen late; I note it and move on.
nap-18100212-462: I beg you send for the Dutch minister. Tell him Police minister had interviews with king of Holland, who desires to conciliate his country independence with my views, proposes: first cede left bank of Rhine to France; second stop all communication with England.
nap-18100223-463: I hasten to inform you the marriage contract between myself and Archduchess Marie Louise, daughter of the Emperor of Austria, was ratified at Vienna. Similar letters to all imperial family.
nap-18100301-464: I attach great importance to Congreve rockets. As soon as fabrication success established, send to Spain against Cadiz, Ciudad-Rodrigo, Badajoz -- forward to seventh and Third Army Corps in Catalonia and Aragon.
nap-18100302-465: I have set the theatre program across the year, with productions planned for spring, Easter, summer, and autumn.
nap-18100403-466: I do not consider it right you should issue a proclamation.
nap-18100425-467: I wrote to send away the Persian ambassador, but without treating him badly. Tell him I do not wish to see him, displeased Persia sold political interests to the English.
nap-18100501-468: You must deny report of Moreau recall, state that general, whose intrigues with Bourbons are well known, is forever excluded from France.
nap-18100501-469: I reckon you will have ten vessels in roads by summer, yet I have heard of no movement in Holland. Think how important this is for the common cause, keep your engagements. POSITION of two brothers: Napoleon hardly seated Louis on Holland throne when quarrels began.
nap-18100501-470: I write to king of Spain: sorry to see extensive arming of Spaniards, only prolongs resistance, causes French blood to flow; when so often deceived difficult to understand such obstinacy.
nap-18100516-471: Caulaincourt informed me of all amiable things your Majesty said on my marriage. Accept my thanks. My feelings towards you as unchangeable as political principles governing my empire relations. Never will your Majesty have to complain of France.
nap-18100518-472: Present lucid note to Prussian ambassador on prince of Hatzfeld affair: dwell on scandal of trial, how it displeases me, I recognise the hand of that cabal drawing down misfortunes.
nap-18100529-473: Inform king of Spain: I cannot send regiment Joseph-Napoleon, animated with such bad spirit officers demanded its withdrawal from Spain frontiers; he can judge how impolitic and inconsiderate his Spanish levies are.
nap-18070826-400: English at Copenhagen, bombarding. Russia should march on Sweden for Denmark. Alexander need only say -- I do all necessary. Army at Hamburg. If English continue: close all European ports, expel ambassadors, arrest individuals. Joint declaration to Austria if Emperor agrees.
nap-18080201-408: Sir my Brother -- Savary arrived, we spoke hours of your Majesty. English parliament continues war. Caulaincourt has my opinion. Only large measures bring peace. Augment your army -- I help fully. No jealousy vs Russia; desire her glory, prosperity, extension.
nap-18080201-409: Courier to Constantinople on Algiers. Turkish ambassador: condescendence for Porte delays expedition; but if slaves not freed by return courier, I seize Algiers.
nap-18080211-410: My Son -- my troops entered Rome on the second, consul and Queen Caroline agents arrested. Write Miollis: take police, treat Papal troops well, drive out Neapolitan rebels, even cardinals.
nap-18080214-411: My Son -- recalled Alquier. Miollis pay difficulties at Rome. Must ensure troops want nothing; if Rome cannot furnish, Miollis takes government and ecclesiastical provinces except Ancona, Camerino, Urbino, Macerata under Lemarrois. Secret: possible I go to Rome soon.
nap-18090101-434: Pope sends tapers. Rome agent: I refuse. Spain refuses. Naples, Holland refuse -- papal court offered none last year. Charge d'affaires: Candlemas I receive tapers blessed by my cure -- not purple or power gives value. Popes and cures in hell; my cure taper as holy.
nap-18090101-435: My Son -- Battaglia: Augusta another princess. I hope next a boy. Ninth: two letters to Spain king -- solemn Madrid entry, well received; councils, ministers administer. Second: English flight, money convoy captured. English full retreat.
nap-18090201-436: Madam my Sister -- your interest in Spanish arms agreeable, thank you. Sorry king health poor, but spring and Geroux waters salutary.
nap-18090225-437: Sir my Brother -- thank you for interest in my return, congratulations on victories. Would have liked your Majesty in good health.
nap-18090301-438: My Son -- Cesarotti history of popes; if shows harm to religion, publish. Next day to German vassals: Vienna news requires contingents without delay.
nap-18100610-474: Report the missing conscripts. I might post them dangerously: ship them to Corsica, form six or seven thousand for Sardinia under a good general and colonels. Idleness breeds desertion; give them an island to take.
nap-18100610-475: I wrote to you yesterday for the letter which M. Fagan brought back from Lord Wellesley. I write to you again today to let you know that you must hand to me, with that letter, all the documents, without exception, concerning Ouvrard, Labouchere, and Fagan.
nap-18100610-476: Instruct Oudinot: once his Utrecht force can march on Amsterdam, let him write my charge that French troops were insulted and Haarlem shut its gates. Demand amends. My eagles enter every friendly land.
nap-18100614-477: I have read your report on the subject of the dispute between my Consul and the Dey of Algiers. My agent seems to me very culpable; he should not compromise my interests for such trifles. Make known to him my displeasure. Let M. Thainville settle this affair.
nap-18100710-480: I plant press pieces on Russian wins in Turkey and the coming peace: Moldavia and Wallachia ceded, and vessels falsely claimed from Teneriffe seized, English goods in truth.
nap-18100720-481: MADAME -- I hasten to inform you that the king of Holland is at Teplitz in Bohemia. As you must have experienced some uneasiness on his disappearance, I do not lose a moment in sending you this news to tranquillise you.
nap-18100721-482: Sir, my Brother and Father-in-Law -- Allow me to send your Imperial majesty a porcelain cup from my manufactory of Sevres upon which the portrait of Louise is painted. I hope that this present will be agreeable to your Majesty, and that you will find it well done.
nap-18100726-483: Have a courier ready to convey my letter to the Emperor of Austria. Write to M. Otto to demand the arrest of Pozzo di Borgo as having been condemned to death by default for having betrayed France in favour of England.
nap-18100726-484: Summon this director to Paris to answer for himself, and report him fully to me. I will know why the Hercule's business miscarried. My service suffers no sleepy agents.
nap-18100819-486: I have received no details respecting my army of Catalonia. I am ignorant of the manner in which Macdonald has made his movement, what troops he has taken with him, and what cantonments he has left behind him. My Army of Catalonia is the only one of which I have no news.
nap-18100822-487: I have received your letter: 200 Englishmen have been removed from the Irish regiment.
nap-18100918-489: I hear everywhere the rumour of Prince Ferdinand's pretended match with an Austrian princess, and I credit it.
nap-18100918-490: I have read with surprise a letter from the major of the Irish regiment. I never ordered that the Irishmen who fought for me at Flushing, and who were wounded in my service, should be sent back among the prisoners. I can therefore understand nothing of this gossip.
nap-18100920-491: Write to Prussia, and speak to M. de Krusemark here, saying that I should like to see the Prussian government lay a duty on the export of cereals. England is in want of corn, and it will be useful and agreeable to Prussia to levy this contribution from her.
nap-18100921-492: The idea of sending Spaniards to Corfu is bad. Give orders for the Spaniards to be sent to Toulon. At Corfu they would consume provisions, and would betray us on the first opportunity. They must be sent into the interior.
nap-18101001-493: If there are any monks among the Spanish prisoners, you must make them throw off their frocks on crossing the frontier, and have them dressed with coats and mixed up with the other prisoners.
nap-18101013-494: I send you a draft of instructions for M. De Nerciat. I wish this agent for the present to visit only Syria and Egypt; he must pay attention to St.
nap-18101014-495: I send you a letter from General Rapp.
nap-18101017-496: I forward a letter, which has just fallen into my hands. Write to M. Otto (ambassador at Vienna) to forewarn him on the subject of the false rumours it contains. Speak in the Moniteur of the presents which I made M.
nap-18101101-497: Have all the merchandise of English manufacture in Holland, in the warehouses, shops, etc., burned at once. My finances are in the most prosperous condition. I can meet all the expenses of this immense empire without demanding any new sacrifices on the part of my people.
nap-18101112-499: Send my Berne minister the Valais reunion decree, sealed till Caesar Berthier plants my troops in Sion and holds the land. Let him call it proof of Swiss freedom, settling Italy and Switzerland for good. I take what the blockade demands.
nap-18101118-500: Send me the draft of a reply to Prince Kourakine, very polite, very moderate, but which nevertheless shall contain those truths which it is fit that Russia should know.
nap-18101201-501: I send you a report on the losses of Westphalia. You argue as if Hanover belonged to Westphalia. Hanover does not belong to the King Jerome, for that prince not having executed the treaty which he concluded with me, I look upon it as null and void.
nap-18110101-503: They have just discovered a party of the Pope here. An Abbe Gregori and an Abbe Fontana, whom I brought here from Rome, were the intermediaries of a correspondence between the Pope and the Vicars-General of Paris.
nap-18110129-504: I send you back your report on Papal affairs; I find it incorrect. For instance, the union of the Papal states to the empire did not take place until the Pope was at Savona. You must not speak of the marriage and the legitimacy of the child; that is too absurd.
nap-18110201-505: Tell the Transport Office: among prisoners sits Kolli, self-styled Irishman, bearing England's letter and a minister's commission to Ferdinand. I will trade him for equal rank.
nap-18110225-506: I have read with attention the letters from Stockholm. There is so much effervescence and turmoil in the head of the prince of Sweden, that I attach no importance to the communication he has addressed to Baron Alquier.
nap-18110301-507: I have received your report on the Irish regiment. Send me a more detailed report, informing me if the officers of that corps are Irish, and if there are means of creating an Irish regiment principally recruited among Germans.
nap-18110310-508: I send a courier to st. Petersburg with a letter from General Lauriston to count romanzoff, announcing his approaching departure, his desire to be agreeable, and the hope that his mission will meet with the approbation of the Czar.
nap-18110402-509: I forward you a report from Marshal Marmont with regard to the request of Prince Schwartzenberg relative to affairs in Illyria. You should see the marshal in order to draw up a reply, and try if it would not be better to settle the mortmain affairs.
nap-18110613-511: I beg that you will write a letter to the transport office, demanding the return to France of all the prisoners who are in England, captured at Baylen with Dupont's army. Put forward some reasons to show how just this would be.
nap-18110621-512: I beg that you will hint gently to the Swedish ambassador that I regret to see the Princess royal arrive in France without having obtained permission; that this is not usual, and that I am sorry she should have left her husband at so critical a moment.
nap-18110704-513: Send for O'Connor and the Paris Irish; raise an Irish party. I hold twenty-five sail in the Scheldt, nine at Texel. I lean to landing thirty thousand foot and four thousand horse. I will sign whatever Ireland asks.
nap-18110801-514: I shall make no difficulty about granting Prussia licences for the exportation of Silesian cloths. Demand that Prussia shall no longer receive any colonial produce coming from Russia.
nap-18110801-515: I send you a letter from a soldier in garrison at Stettin. He says that there are a great many men on the sick list. I thought that the air of Stettin was good. Take care to have my Troops quartered in places where no sickness is to be feared.
nap-18110801-516: Let me know what day my troops can embark at Cherbourg. When will all the vessels be there? I have a great many relations with Ireland. I already hold the thread which sets a good many things in motion. My agents begin to come and go.
nap-18110823-518: Rate Soult through Berthier: sending Albuera trophies by an Austrian hireling insults me. The fellow fought against us. I expect my marshals to know their messengers.
nap-18110824-519: It is necessary for you to write again to my minister at Carlsruhe. The Princess Stephanie is wrong to show a preference for Manheim; her duty is to be with her husband.
nap-18110918-521: I have read with interest the letter of General O'Connor, which I return. It appears very important to me to establish relations with Ireland. Ask for particulars with regard to the state of public opinion at present.
nap-18111026-522: From this place I intend going to the Grand Duchy of Berg, and afterwards to Fontainebleau. I am extremely satisfied with the Dutch.
nap-18111101-523: I beg that you will see the queen of Spain and Tell her that I wish the princess of Sweden to leave Paris and return to Stockholm.
nap-18111101-524: I am informed that you have made a present of some horses to the Prince royal of Sweden. I desire that you countermand the despatch of these horses. Sweden is behaving very badly, and at any moment we may go to war. These gifts are therefore not proper at the present moment.
nap-18111206-525: Nesselrode's coming decides me: I raise the conscription. Bid the Confederation princes remount horse and ready contingents, pleading Russia's mass levy, her crowded frontier, her bent for war. To my foreign minister: in war Bignon joins my staff to head secret police.
nap-18120106-527: In the Reveries of Marshal Saxe, amid a great many things extremely mediocre, there are some ideas on the way of raising contributions in the enemy's country without fatiguing the army, which appear to me to be good.
nap-18120108-528: I await with impatience your report upon the colonial merchandise which you have found in Pomerania. You have, no doubt, sent a detachment of custom-house officers there.
nap-18120114-529: You have given the command of the department of the Apennines to Adjutant Commander Bourmont, that is to say to an old Chouan leader. This measure is ridiculous. That officer should not be employed, or employed only in such a way as to be under supervision.
nap-18120202-530: The reports from Toulon, as well as accounts from England, show that my squadron manoeuvred badly, and that it ought to have captured two English frigates which were allowed to escape.
nap-18120216-531: I m. Is not fit for the foreign office. He is said to be imbued with English customs and tastes, and that he likes and prefers the individuals of that nation to other people. This, in a French agent, is very inconvenient. M.
nap-18120227-532: I send you the papers of the Committee of inquiry on the capitulation of Dupont at Baylen, I beg that you will read them with care and draw up a report. You must join to the report a demand on the part of Comte Regnaud for the convocation of the High court.
nap-18120301-533: It is time to finish with this scandal of the Sisters of Charity who have revolted against the Superioresses. It is my intention to suppress the convents which, within twenty-four hours after being warned, have not submitted.
nap-18120312-535: Tell Marmont: holding five English divisions beyond the Tagus clears him; if Badajos falls to two, blame the south army alone. I judge commanders by results.
nap-18120328-536: I send you a report on the Russian army furnished by the Prussians. Ask Prince Schwartzenberg to communicate to you the ideas of Vienna upon it. It seems to me that this report gives three divisions too many.
nap-18120616-538: I tell you Ney corps strays from its traced route, ravaging everywhere.
nap-18120702-540: Today our van seized eight guns and seven hundred men. Russia lies at Vitebsk. I tell you privately, write nothing of it. We stand on the edge of great events.
nap-18120801-541: I have this instant returned to my quarters; the heat is excessive, and there is a great deal of dust, which fatigues us a little. We had the whole Russian army here; it received orders to deliver battle, and did not dare. We carried Smolensko by assault.
nap-18120826-543: The enemy, after having constructed fortifications, raised batteries and redoubts, and announced their intention of making a stand here, as usual, failed in resolution. We entered this town, which is considerable enough, as it has eight or ten steeples.
nap-18120902-545: I have received the report of Marshal Marmont on the battle of Salamanca. It is impossible to read anything more paltry; there is more noise and more clatter in it than in a clock, and not a word to explain the real state of affairs.
nap-18120910-546: It is supposed that Wittgenstein has left the Drissa in order to take up a position between Moscow and St. Petersburg. Should this turn out to be true, write to Marshal St. Cyr to pursue him, and to arrive at the same time as the enemy, in order to cover my flank.
nap-18121010-548: I on the or Marshal Mortier must set fire to the eau-de-vie stores, the barracks, and to the public establishments, with the exception of the foundling hospital. He must set fire to the palace of the Kremlin.
nap-18121016-549: I am indebted to you for the excellent care you take of the little king, and I am deeply grateful.
nap-18121102-550: I have received your letter. You say nothing about France and give me no news of Spain; I have had no dispatches for a fortnight and remain in the dark.
nap-18121214-554: I pause at Dresden to write to your Majesty. Despite my fatigue, my health is excellent. I left Lithuania after the battle of the Beresina, leaving the Grand Army under the King of Naples.
nap-18121218-555: We are terribly fatigued and half starved. Send bread, meat, and brandy to meet us. I have 100,000 stragglers who are trying to live, and who are no longer under the colours. This causes us to run horrible dangers. My Old guard alone maintains its ranks, but hunger is gaining it.
nap-18121218-556: Most Holy Father, I send my household officer with joy at your mending health; summer alarms proved hollow. Your new residence lets us meet; despite all, my friendship stands.
nap-18130101-557: Send Duroc for the inventor; prove his musket with my Guard gunners, trial it, report to me. I love a new arm.
nap-18130101-558: According to custom, I consider it right, on important occasions, to make known our situation to your Majesty. Your Majesty has learned from the published reports the victories which I have gained over the Russian armies. I did not once meet them without beating them.
nap-18130101-559: I have received your letter. I am pleased to see the army command in your hands. The King of Naples has acted so extravagantly that I have nearly arrested him as an example.
nap-18130107-560: Boulogne camp dissolves; quarter the troops in town. To Berthier: yours with its strange news received. York's treason decides me. I speak to the nation and ordain a mighty levy. I form an army of observation.
nap-18130126-561: All your efforts should tend towards preserving Warsaw.
nap-18130131-562: I have repeated my orders for the King of Spain to move his headquarters to Valladolid, hold Madrid with only his left flank, and send forces to subdue northern Spain.
nap-18130201-563: The viceroy writes to me that General Bülow has only 300 cavalry, and that therefore Prussia, instead of joining with us to defend her territory, and to repair the treason of General York, does nothing.
nap-18130202-564: I have ordered Admiral Baste to command the flotilla in Swedish Pomerania and defend Rügen and the coast. He must inspect the mouths of the Oder.
nap-18130210-565: Her hopes know no bounds. She barters my finest provinces for treason and prices peace at my Empire's dismemberment. I read the offer plain and I refuse it.
nap-18130218-566: England fattens Portugal to thrust into Spain or land on my coast while I face north. Warn Spain's king: he squandered idle months when England could do nothing, never taming Navarre, Biscay, Aragon. Ever begging coin, he lets Mina waste my provinces.
nap-18130301-567: I beg that you will let me know if my palaces of Strasburg and of Mayence are in a good condition. They may be useful either for me or for the families of some of the princes of the confederation.
nap-18130302-568: I have received your letter from Leipsic. As soon as you receive news of General Morand, let me know, even the rumours which may reach you. By our latest news it appears still undecided whether Prussia will take the field against us.
nap-18130312-569: Magdeburg must live by requisition, as war has always allowed; Italy in my last campaign, Strasburg and Mayence lived so. Do there what I did there. You dream millions while I count the cost of three hundred thousand men.
nap-18130313-570: I return you the letter of the Bishop of Nantes. You must inform him that the form of the oath cannot be changed; that it could only be changed if it contained anything contrary to the mysteries of religion. All the pretensions of the cardinals are ridiculous.
nap-18130313-571: I approve of the measures taken for the defence of the Pyrenees, and for calling out the National guard.
nap-18130401-572: I grieve for Dresden bridge, Davoust's blast, yet money mends what powder breaks; some hundred thousand francs. To Jerome I wrote the same lesson: war devours coin, count it closely.
nap-18130401-573: I have reason to be satisfied with the intentions of Austria. I do not suspect her preparations; however, it is not my intention to be dependent upon her. The vulnerable part as regards Austria is my kingdom of Italy whither I intend to send the viceroy as soon as possible.
nap-18130402-574: Tell Spain's king I gave him my armies' chief command; his endless disobeyed complaints come from mixing Spain's king with my generalissimo. My armies answer no Spanish minister. From France expect nothing now.
nap-18130413-575: These are the plans for my departure; I shall start with you in a light carriage; the Grand marshal and the Comte de Lobau in another carriage; Fain and Yvan in a third. The three carriages must be all equally light.
nap-18130417-576: I reached Mayence in forty hours, in good health and without accident. The carriage of the Grand marshal has not yet rejoined me. I shall remain here for several days to look after a great many things which are wanting. To Berthier: send a courier to the king of Bavaria.
nap-18130418-577: I send you a letter from Comte de Mercy. I am extremely dissatisfied with the manner in which I am seconded by my Minister of Foreign affairs (M. Maret, due de Bassano).
nap-18130420-578: I have received your letter. The rumors about the King of Saxony’s fidelity are absurd; neither his opinions nor his probity are known. Deny these rumors firmly.
nap-18130501-579: Sir, my Brother, and very dear Father-in-Law, What your Majesty said in your letter on the subject of the interest you bear me greatly affected me. I deserve this in consequence of my loyal feeling towards you.
nap-18130503-580: I am sorry that you did not advise the Empress to pardon the man condemned to death. You acted too much like a magistrate in that affair. Take the first opportunity of making the Empress accord one or two pardons on her own initiative.
nap-18130507-581: Send the inclosed letter to M. de Serra at Prague. The Emperor has arrived at Dresden. Tomorrow the army will pass the river in pursuit of the enemy. Inclosed you will find a letter on the subject of the conduct of General Thielman. You must tell M.
nap-18130510-582: Dresden is mine, both banks and Elbe forts; Silesia next, likely. Long disgraced, Fouche gets my secret call: entering Prussia, I set him over its rule. Lutzen drove them over the river. Come at once; the Regent alone knows.
nap-18130512-583: I delivered battle to the Russian and Prussian army entrenched at Bautzen and Hochkirch. Providence granted me victory; my health is excellent.
nap-18130601-584: I have seen with pleasure that amidst the vicissitudes of political events the feelings of your Majesty have remained unchangeable. The evil intentions of Sweden towards me are the result of my constant refusal to adhere to the spoliation of Norway.
nap-18130602-585: You will see by the Moniteur that negotiations for an armistice are going on. It will probably be signed tomorrow or the day after. This armistice interferes with the course of my victories.
nap-18130607-586: I see with pleasure that my Son grows and continues to give hopes. I can but express my satisfaction for all the care you bestow upon him. The death of the due de Frioul pained me. This was the only time during twenty years that he did not guess what would please me.
nap-18130608-587: Play season sleeps; send at most six or seven picked players for as many pieces. No fuss, no roadside pomp. Yet let Paris buzz as if the whole tragedy sails, gossip serves me. Remusat chooses the troupe.
nap-18130630-588: Prince Metternich has handed me your Majesty's letter. I desire peace. If the Russians show themselves as moderate as I am it will be promptly concluded.
nap-18130701-589: Since war opened the allies never won so full a victory, against all our united strength, utterly overturning us. I record the disaster plainly; it shall be answered.
nap-18130717-590: I consider the Bishop of Nantes the Empire’s most enlightened priest and one of the Sorbonne’s finest doctors.
nap-18130801-591: If I were at Paris, I should go to Cherbourg to be present at the introduction of the sea. I wish the Empress to go there, and, if she goes, it will be proper for you to accompany her. The marine might order something to do honour to the Empress and to amuse her.
nap-18130801-592: To Drouot: present my actors' bounty plan; Turenne ships the troupe home. To Cambaceres: see Savary, I gave him my view of things. Austria shall rue her folly and treason; I expect the truce denounced and her declaration within days.
nap-18130801-593: I fear Austria’s declaration of war will bring costly battles. The unexpected turn in Spain also makes securing the frontier essential.
nap-18130807-594: Austria fields three hundred thousand: one hundred twenty thousand on Dresden, twenty thousand on Bavaria, fifty thousand on my viceroy. Oudinot, Vandamme, Regnier and Padoue debouch eighty thousand by Luckau and Bayreuth for Berlin.
nap-18130817-595: I have long thought that Caulaincourt and de Narbonne allow themselves to be taken in by the honeyed style of Metternich.
nap-18130826-596: I informed you of my intentions yesterday. The whole army of the enemy presented itself before Dresden yesterday, and Marshal St. Cyr feared that he would be attacked today; I am going there.
nap-18130901-598: Macdonald wavers at Gorlitz; must I ride to prop him? Vandamme's ruin beggars belief: no sentry, no reserve, yet the chief, they say, destroyed himself. His men pour back, generals and fifteen thousand with them; I count my loss a few thousand.
nap-18130902-599: Write thus to Marshal Ney: We have just received news from Marshal Oudinot who deemed fit to venture within two marches of Wittenberg.
nap-18130919-600: I general bruno was captured, not by 4,000, but by 400 men, while he was quietly sleeping in the town, with his whole force. As long as the light troops perform their duties so badly accidents will happen.
nap-18131007-601: I wrote to you this morning at one o'clock. I am starting for Meissen. The whole Silesian army has debouched by Wartenburg; there is no force from Dresden to Gorlitz, nor from Dresden to Berlin. Marshal St. Cyr will remain at Dresden.
nap-18131031-602: I have arrived here. The Bavarians and Austrians, 60,000 strong, posted at Hanau, tried to cut me off from France. I gave them a good drubbing, and captured their guns, standards, and 6,000 prisoners. My health was never better. I am going to Mayence.
nap-18131110-603: I am not aware if Belfort is in a state of defence. If so, have it armed, as well as all the castles along the Swiss frontier. Not that I have any reason to distrust the Swiss, but because in the present state of the empire it is necessary to arm on all sides.
nap-18131110-604: Give orders that if ever the English arrive at the castle of Marracq near Bayonne it be set fire to; also to all the houses which belong to me, so that they may not sleep in my bed.
nap-18131110-605: The movement of the English upon Bayonne has opened up a portion of the frontier. I learn that they have already landed a certain quantity of their merchandise near St. Jean-de-Luz. I suppose that you have removed your custom-house line. This matter deserves your attention.
nap-18140101-606: I consider it doubtful if the allies are acting in good faith, and if England desires peace. For myself I desire it, but solid and honourable. France without her natural limits, without Ostend and Antwerp, would not be on an equal footing with the other states of Europe.
nap-18140101-607: You will have seen, by the various documents which have been published, all the efforts made to obtain peace. I have since sent my Minister of Foreign affairs to the enemy's outposts. They put off receiving him and yet they march forward.
nap-18140110-609: I have had it placed in the orders of the palace that you shall henceforth be announced as King Joseph, and the queen as the Queen Julie, with all the honours, and in the manner usual with French princes.
nap-18140110-610: Bulow floods Belgium with twenty thousand, nine thousand of them Graham's English. Meet him with all you have. I trust your vigour where others temporize.
nap-18140116-611: PRINCE, The delays which have taken place in the negotiations are due neither to France nor to Austria, and yet France and Austria suffer the most from them. The allied armies have already invaded several of our provinces.
nap-18140201-612: Berthier sent you a courier from the field of battle. I have since despatched the young Montesquiou. It is 8 o'clock, and before going to sleep I send you two words to inform you that the affair of yesterday was decisive. The enemy's army of Silesia no longer exists.
nap-18140201-613: It is necessary that the vice-reine should go to Paris without delay in order to be confined, it being my intention that, under no circumstances, shall she remain in a country occupied by the enemy.
nap-18140201-614: What! Six hours after having received the first troops coming from Spain you were not in the field! Six hours' repose was sufficient. I won the action of Nangis with a brigade of dragoons coming from Spain, which, since it left Bayonne, had not unbridled its horses.
nap-18140201-615: I write to Marshal Soult that with his fine troops he ought to beat the Duke of Wellington, but that under present circumstances a little more decision and vigour are necessary.
nap-18140204-616: The report of Prince Schwartzenberg is a piece of folly. There has been no battle. The Old guard was not there; the Young guard was not engaged. A few guns were taken from us by charges of cavalry.
nap-18140206-617: I am much surprised that Marshal Suchet should not have despatched the troops which I demanded from Lyons. They ought to have arrived and I hear no more of them. If the marshal has taken upon himself not to execute orders he is very culpable.
nap-18140207-618: I see that instead of sustaining the Empress you discourage her. Why do you lose your head like that? What are these Misereres, and these prayers of forty hours at the chapel? Have people in Paris gone mad?
nap-18140207-619: I see with pleasure the advantages which you have obtained; if they had been a little more decisive we should have been able to keep Italy. I have destroyed the army of Silesia, composed of Russians and Prussians. I began yesterday to beat Schwartzenberg.
nap-18140210-620: I have just arrived at Nogent. The enemy after Montereau fell back upon Troyes with the greater portion of their army. They enjoyed great luck, for the frost enabled them to march across country; but for this half their baggage and their artillery would have been captured.
nap-18140214-621: I send you a line to let you know the happy issue of the battle of Vauchamps.
nap-18140301-623: I put the following note in the Moniteur: the Emperor had his head-quarters on the at berry-au-bac.
nap-18140301-624: Find Suchet's ten thousand; post five or six thousand to the Dordogne. I need my southern door barred.
nap-18140302-626: Write to Marshal Soult that with troops like his he should beat the enemy, if he will only exhibit pluck and place himself at the head of the troops. Let him understand that we have reached a period when more than ordinary resolution and vigour are required.
nap-18140303-627: Before commencing the fortifications of Paris the plan must be known; that which has been presented to me appears to be very complicated; more simplicity is required.
nap-18140310-628: The army which I beat at Craonne was the Russian army. It lost heavily, and fell back upon Laon, where it was joined by the corps of Bulow, York, and Kleist, forming the Prussian army.
nap-18140314-629: I have arrived at Rheims, which General St. Priest had occupied with three Russian divisions and a Prussian division which had just arrived from Stettin. I beat them; I retook the town, 20 guns, a great deal of baggage, and made 5,000 prisoners. General St.
nap-18140315-630: Marshal Mortier writes that the enemy are in full retreat, and seem to be falling back upon Laon. I have sent some cavalry to follow their march, which is being made in good order. Send some peasants to try and find out if the enemy are in force at Craonne.
nap-18140318-631: Write to Soissons to inform General Moreau, who commands there, that I have reached Fismes, and to tell him to send me news of Marshals Marmont and Mortier, who were to march upon Soissons. He must also tell me what he knows of the movements of the enemy.
nap-18140318-632: Yesterday I beat Winzingerode, Langeron, and Woronsow, united, with the remains of Sacken's army. I made 2,000 prisoners. The battle of Craonne is glorious. Marshals Victor and Grouchy were wounded. I have 700 or 800 killed or wounded.
nap-18140320-633: Yesterday I crossed the Aube at Plancy, and at once marched upon Mery. I attacked the town, which was carried by evening.
nap-18140323-634: I send disguised gendarmes to Metz, Bar and Nancy with my letters to the mayors.
nap-18140401-635: I have received your letter. Your conduct during these difficult times has pleased me; I thank you, and it confirms my good opinion of your character.
nap-18140408-636: I ordered Marmont, Mortier, Oudinot, Serrurier, Belliard, Gérard, Sorbier, and Sebastiani to report to the palace at ten tonight and return to their posts before daybreak.
nap-18140610-637: It is my intention to appoint the mayor of Porto Longone commandant of my palace at Porto Longone. He must perform the functions of commandant, concierge, keeper of the robes, and overseer of the gardens. He will receive a salary of 600 francs.
nap-18140818-638: Colonel Laczinski, who is going to leave today for Leghorn, will go from there to Aix, and will take with him a letter from me to the Empress.
nap-18140826-639: I think that I asked you to write to the Princess Pauline not to bring her piano master with her, but only a good singer and a good songstress, seeing that we have here a good violin player and a good pianist.
nap-18150301-642: FRENCHMEN, The defection of Marshal Augereau delivered Lyons, without defence, to our enemies. The army which I confided to him was strong enough to beat the Austrians, and to fall upon the rear of the left wing of the army which threatened Paris.
nap-18150301-643: I have arrived. I have traversed France. The army and the people of country and of town came out to meet me. I entered Paris on the at the head of the camp of Essonne, upon which the king counted.
nap-18150410-644: You must efface Berthier, Marmont, Victor, Perignon, Augereau, and Kellermann from the list of marshals. You must present me a report, so that a pension may be granted to those marshals who have no fortune.
nap-18150426-645: Tell Marshal Suchet, if he is still at Lyons, to remain there, and if he has left send him a courier, so that he may return. I give the command of the army of the Alps definitively to that marshal.
nap-18150527-646: The Guard may soon march, leaving Paris without troops. I want the National Guard officers commissioned before the Guard departs.
nap-18150601-647: Enclosed you will find a copy of the orders which I have given for the cavalry of the army. Marshal Grouchy will command it in chief. Give him a chief of the staff, and a general of artillery. All the generals on the unattached list are at his service.
nap-18150601-648: I have told Marshal Suchet to seize Montmélian when hostilities open, unless enemy movements force an earlier move; if possible, wait one more day.
nap-18150601-649: I am moving my headquarters to Beaumont tonight. Tomorrow I will move to Charleroi, where the Prussian army is; this may bring a battle or force its retreat.
nap-18150606-650: My dream is France as free as may be; I say may be, for anarchy always hatches absolute rule. Two hundred guns must crown the gates and works of Paris within days. Tell me when the first naval pieces arrive.
nap-18150616-651: I send you my aide-de-camp, General Flahault, with the present letter. I wish to write to you in detail because it is of the greatest importance. Marshal Grouchy is marching on Sombreffe with the third and fourth corps of infantry.
nap-17910123-01: From Bonifacio to Cape Corse, from Ajaccio to Bastia, nothing rises but a chorus of curses against you. Your friends hide, your kin disown you. You have ruined Corsica; you have sold its honour to the French.
nap-17931207-01: I have received your letters. We remain in much the same position, with 30,000 troops and eleven batteries against Fort Malbousquet. The siege continues.
nap-17931224-02: I promised you brilliant successes, and you see I keep my word. Worn out with fatigue and work, I could not tell you first; suffice it that the English carried off none of our guns. The defence holds firm.
nap-17940104-01: Fort Saint-Nicolas cannot withstand a quarter-hour. The three walls closing it town-side are razed. I am pushing the works forward with all speed. The enemy will find no shelter there.
nap-17940228-03: More grain ships came into the roads this evening; but the enemy squadron keeps them from venturing through. I shall have two batteries built which, once finished, will make coastal traffic safe, under the very eyes of the enemy squadron.
nap-17940407-02: I order: Rebuild Sainte-Marguerite point battery; raise the mortar parapet eight feet. The works must be completed before the enemy can react. Speed is everything in these preparations.
nap-17940521-03: I say: Piedmont plain demands superior force; join the Alps and Italy armies for it. A divided command will fail; unity of effort is the only path to victory in that theatre.
nap-17940620-04: I set the plan: 1. Secure rearwards against enemies within and without. 2. Unite the Alps and Italy defence systems. 3. Concentrate artillery where it can strike the decisive blow. These are the pillars.
nap-17940627-05: Call it not Pelletier but Marguerite island; renaming places needs a Convention decree. I insist on the proper forms; revolutionary nomenclature must follow the law.
nap-17940702-06: The Republic breeds two alarmists: grain-famine criers and powder-fearers. Both spread panic to serve their own ends. I will not tolerate defeatism disguised as caution.
nap-17940702-07: It is imposture to claim 28 thousand powder at Antibes when you hold 45. I know the true state of the magazines; false returns will be punished severely.
nap-17940915-08: I wrote you several times unanswered; I cannot think it contempt. Perhaps my letters miscarried, but silence from a subordinate is not acceptable. Respond at once.
nap-17950601-33: I intend to use all haste with the commissions for your wife. Desiree demands my portrait; you will give it to her should she still wish for it; if not, keep it for yourself. Family matters must not distract from duty.
nap-17950618-09: Never take me for a dupe; these twenty days I know Saliceti hides with you. I see through the manoeuvres of those who think themselves clever. The truth will out.
nap-17950622-10: Your No. 16 received. Chiappe's letter pleased me. I shall do what I can for Lucien. Brother, your requests find a willing ear when they serve the cause.
nap-17950701-19: I am a general employed in the army of the West; my malady detains me here. I await further details from you. I believe you avoid speaking to me about Desiree on purpose.
nap-17950712-11: I say the English must re-embark within days. Pichegru prepares the Rhine crossing. The Vendée is quiet. The Chouans only north of the Loire. Peace with Spain is imminent.
nap-17950712-18: I report: English will re-embark in days. Pichegru prepares Rhine crossing. La Vendee tranquil, Chouans only north of Loire. Peace with Spain imminent. Dutch warm friends of Revolution. Italy grows rich on France spoils. Luxury and arts flourish astonishingly.
nap-17950724-12: I did not write, friend, for I had no pleasant news to give. Silence is sometimes the only honest report when affairs go ill.
nap-17950728-13: Twelve thousand émigrés landed at Quiberon, battering the isthmus passage. The Royalist invasion has begun; we must crush it before it spreads.
nap-17950817-20: I congratulate you on joining the army. Fortune, favour, esteem of men vary perpetually. I have been appointed general of the Line in La Vendee: I have not accepted. Many would command a brigade better; few command artillery so well.
nap-17950823-14: The Committee sent you, general, by last courier, Italy's direction instructions. You will execute them without delay. The army of Italy awaits your orders.

nap-17961004-17: Modena's armistice conditions stand unfulfilled. I hold them to their word.

nap-17971117-169: Cisalpine Republic, we gave you liberty; guard it. To deserve your fate make only wise, honourable laws and enforce them hard. Spread knowledge, honour religion. I trust your future to you.

nap-17980106-05: Months ago I sent two deputies to the Maniots. The Greek allies await my direction.

nap-17980124-10: I received your letter announcing your Departure for Rome. Arrive as fast as you can. The march on Rome cannot wait.

nap-17990602-12: Leave at Qatyeh all Christians sheltered with us from Acre or Jaffa. The protected civilians remain in safety.
nap-17990602-13: I have stationed the first battalion of the Third at Fort El-Arich until further orders.
nap-17990615-14: I thank General Dugua for his conduct during my absence in Syria.
nap-17990615-15: I arrived yesterday with part of the army. I left a good garrison in Fort El-Arich. The return to Egypt is complete.
nap-17990617-16: I am sending General Desaix to Rahyreh province; the naval legion will leave Rosetta.
nap-17990619-17: I learned with pleasure your occupation of Qoseyr. Engineers are ordered to you. The Red sea port is secured.
nap-17990621-18: Yesterday I inspected Cairo citadel myself; Citizen Fauvi takes an improper tone with the commandant. I correct the insubordination personally.
nap-17990622-19: I inspected the citadel works and commend Brigade Chief Dupas’s extraordinary activity.
nap-17990623-20: Hassan-Toubar leaves me. Tonight he hands over his son as hostage, a man of thirty. The tribal alliance is secured by the hostage.
nap-17990701-34: There is no God but God, and Mohammed is his prophet. To the Divan of Cairo, wisest and most enlightened: I pray the Prophet's grace be on you. Eighty vessels showed before Alexandria; warmly met, they anchor at Aboukir landing troops.
nap-17990702-93: Your Messidor letter is here, with Friant's. I note both. Correspondence with my generals is current.
nap-17990703-94: Your El-Senytali letter received; all cavalry in Bahyreh. The horse is concentrated where needed.
nap-17990704-95: I have ended the customs farm at Qoseyr; the Suez customs rules now apply there.
nap-17990705-96: I friant: Mourad still at hayan fountain. Drive him out. The rebel chief must be pursued.
nap-17990707-97: Your report is here; Mourad never left the Rayan springs. I see the foe sits fast. Hold him under your eye.
nap-17990709-98: Both your letters are here. I read them with attention. The intelligence is noted; carry on.
nap-17990709-99: Your two Talia letters are here; we must concentrate. I order the forces gathered for the next blow.
nap-17990801-174: Europe's news sends me to France. I leave Kleber my army. You shall hear from me soon. It rends me to quit troops I love. Italy is lost; Mantua, Turin, Tortona invested. Starved of succour and scourged by plague, you may treat with Turkey, even to quitting Egypt.
nap-17990801-35: I have not been well satisfied with your operations during the movements which have just taken place. No matter what events arise, nothing should hinder a soldier from obeying orders; talent in war consists in overcoming obstacles, not causing failure.
nap-17990802-100: I have taken Aboukir fort, the enemy’s battle reserve.
nap-17990804-101: Aboukir summoned; the pasha's son will yield. I grant the capitulation.
nap-17990811-102: Little satisfied with all your operations in this movement. Desaix, your performance disappoints me.
nap-17990811-103: On Syria return you would pass 150,000 livres to the paymaster. The financial obligation stands.
nap-17990811-104: I extremely displeased with zajonchek's negligent execution. The subordinate failed his duty.
nap-17990811-105: Your 18 Thermidor received; projects fully approved. Desaix, this time your plans have my full backing.
nap-17990812-106: Keep my guides and crews. Lannes, the essential personnel stay with the command.
nap-17990822-36: You will find inclosed, Citizen general, an order to take over the command in chief of the army. The fear of English cruisers returning makes me hasten my departure. I take with me Berthier, Lannes, Murat, Andreossy, and Marmont, the citizens Monge and Berthollet.
nap-17990822-81: I take with me Berthier, Lannes, Murat, Andreossy, and Marmont, the citizens Monge and Berthollet. The core staff departs with me for France.
nap-17991010-37: Citizen Directors, since I left France I have received only one of your despatches, which reached me when I was before Acre. It contained the news of our successes at Naples, which made me conjecture an approaching war on the Continent.
nap-17991101-175: Army of the East: France acknowledged all the influence of your conquests on the restoration of her trade and civilization of the world. The eyes of all Europe are upon you, and in thought I am often with you. The Republic honours your service in the East.
nap-18000102-21: I have sent the draft rules for reorganizing the Paris National Guard to the Interior section.
nap-18000104-22: I whereas Brigade chief dupuy, dead arms in hand at Cairo, commanded the through five campaigns. The fallen hero is honoured.
nap-18000104-23: I am satisfied with your conduct in the division. Enlighten the people; Let all citizens feel that parties and strife are past. The division commander earns my confidence.
nap-18000105-24: Tell me Pichegru's conduct abroad since 18 Fructidor Year V. Truth is wanted, not calumny. The Consul demands facts, not slander.
nap-18000105-25: You asked 15,000 men. Consul Bonaparte charges me to answer by extraordinary courier. The First Consul directs the war effort.
nap-18000108-26: Chouan bands gather in Orne. The First Consul complains of hearing nothing from you. The rebellion in the west demands attention.
nap-18000108-27: I want the War Minister to report immediately on the state of the clothing administration.
nap-18000109-28: I saw with indignation that Chouans have settled at Saint-Jean-de-Margon.
nap-18000109-29: I have ordered General Gardanne and the England Army officers to be ready to embark before the month ends.
nap-18000501-38: I have just received your letter of the Floreal.
nap-18000601-176: Soldiers: When we began our march, one department of France was in the hands of the enemy. Consternation pervaded the south of the Republic. You advanced. Joy and hope in our country have succeeded to consternation and fear.
nap-18000601-178: Sire, amid my wounded and fifteen thousand corpses I beg you hear humanity: let not two brave nations cut throats for others' interests. I write from the field itself.
nap-18000620-39: Write to General Kleber that when the news of the capitulation arrived, the Brest squadron was about to sail with 4,000 troops and war stores; we have only just learned the capitulation has been broken, and he has reconquered Egypt.
nap-18000621-40: I ask you to invite two leading singers to Paris for an Italian duet at the national fête. Provide for their travel; I have chosen Madame Billington and Madame Grassini.
nap-18000922-81: I refused ratification of the peace preliminaries after intrigues by the faction opposed to peace.
nap-18010102-01: I legislators, the Republic triumphs. Hohenlinden's victory resounded through Europe. The French arms have prevailed.
nap-18010104-02: I have ordered the Navy Minister to arrest Citizen Tallien, who is accused of leaving Egypt without a passport.
nap-18010107-03: I hand m. De muzquiz a letter complaining of changed preparations against Portugal. The diplomatic pressure on Lisbon continues.
nap-18010107-04: I have told General Menou that Aboukir is the only place for a serious landing in Egypt.
nap-18010109-05: I thank you for your news of the extraordinary 3 Nivose event. The Consul acknowledges the report.
nap-18010109-06: I forty men leave bicetre tomorrow for orleans, thence to embark at Nantes. The conscripts move to the embarkation port.
nap-18010113-07: Brune putting Tuscany under your orders seems to me extremely wise. The command structure in Italy is rationalised.
nap-18010114-08: I a law will Let Ajaccio sell lands to bring water. The birthplace of the Consul gets its aqueduct.
nap-18010114-09: I combis's mission: remind santo domingo's people the land is now French. The colony remembers its allegiance.
nap-18010114-10: I general toussaint louverture, amid revolutionary storms, saved France a great colony by prudence and courage. The black general earns the consul's respect.
nap-18010119-11: I draft a treaty for helvetia to cede all Valais to brigg. The Swiss cantons yield territory to France.
nap-18010121-12: I yesterday a Russian courier arrived in fifteen days with an extremely friendly letter. The czar's overture is welcome.
nap-18010204-13: I dispatch a night courier to General Murat, reaching foligno tomorrow. The urgent orders ride through the night.
nap-18010302-14: Send Madrid the great interest I take in Spain's navy acting again. The Spanish fleet must return to the seas.
nap-18010302-15: I am sending Brigade Chief Savary to Lorient without delay.
nap-18010402-16: We Consuls have found major discrepancies in the military accountants’ ledgers. I want them reconciled.
nap-18010503-17: I several of georges's band wish to submit. The chouan rebels seek amnesty.
nap-18010504-18: I have ordered the War Minister to gather battalions at Brest.
nap-18010601-35: I see with pleasure that you are ready to sail. Your arrival in the Mediterranean is all the more important because the English are preparing to reinforce their army at Aboukir. The fleet must contest the Eastern Mediterranean.
nap-18010602-19: I notify by express that moncey commands French troops in Cisalpine. The command appointment is announced at speed.
nap-18010702-20: I tell him: 'doge' and 'podestat' suit liguria better. The ligurian constitution reflects its own traditions.
nap-18010704-21: I have sent the frigates Bravoure, Carrère, and Succès to Livorno to cruise.
nap-18010806-22: I tell journalists, political and literary, to abstain from all religious matter. The Press must not inflame theological disputes.
nap-18010806-23: I send levavasseur post to Brest to inspect coast batteries. The coastal defences are inspected.
nap-18010905-24: I have ordered the Year X army organization updated without changing soldiers’ pay.
nap-18010905-25: I read the committee's observations; nothing reasonable in them. The Consul dismisses the committee's critique.
nap-18011003-26: I have the salines' receipts. Warn the farmers the government watches. The salt monopoly is enforced.
nap-18011004-27: I have ordered Theophilanthrope societies to stop meeting in national buildings.
nap-18011006-28: I have a handy medium saber modelled. The cavalry weapon is standardised.
nap-18011108-29: I saint-domingue's people, whatever origin or color, are all Frenchmen, all free, all equal before God and Republic. Liberty, equality, fraternity for all.
nap-18011109-30: Frenchmen, yours at last entire, this peace earned by such long generous efforts! The Amiens peace is won by your sacrifices.
nap-18011202-31: I tell montchoisy Paris disowns the Helvetic government. The Swiss puppet regime has no French backing.
nap-18011204-32: I citizen sage reports volta's hard case at Paris. The scientist's situation is reviewed.
nap-18020202-30: I am sending Citizen Lebrun to Turin tonight with the enclosed letter for General Jourdan.
nap-18020202-31: I hasten to Tell Your Holiness the Cisalpine Republic's affairs are arranged. The Italian Sister Republic is settled.
nap-18020202-32: General Silly reports Your Majesty's welcome to 300 French forced by sea onto Sicily. The Neapolitan king shows hospitality to our castaways.
nap-18020202-33: Your 12 Pluviose letter received. All moves at Amiens. Eight days more or less are now indifferent. The peace negotiations proceed at their own pace.
nap-18020205-34: I am considering the minister’s proposal to confirm Fournier’s promotion despite his shortfall in seniority.
nap-18020206-35: I have ordered the memoirs, plans, and scientific findings from the Egypt expedition published at government expense.
nap-18020207-36: I am sending Citizen Lauriston to Brest to await the departure of Bouvet’s squadron.
nap-18020210-37: Glad to read you firmly constituted. You are a small state; live tranquil; shun faction. Lucca's independence depends on unity.
nap-18020607-81: A Barbary ship has been blockading a dozen Ligurian vessels at St. Tropez, and the Maritime Prefect has done nothing to disengage the port. It is a dishonour to the Republic that these Barbary wretches should insult our Coasts.
nap-18020906-81: I send you a note forwarded by the Inspector general of Gendarmery concerning the Bishop of Rennes.
nap-18021202-38: I propose that six bishops remain in Piedmont, using France’s one-bishop-per-two-departments rule as a guide.
nap-18021202-39: I report on wood-cutting bills as paper money. The forest revenue is audited.
nap-18021202-40: I direct only Germinal and Messidor timber receipts to fund Year XI; the rest to Year XII.
nap-18021202-41: I want General Brune to demand the immediate return of Citizen Ruffin’s ship, seized by Djezzar-Pasha.
nap-18021204-42: I have given Beauvoisin all his copies of the Ambigu and the Ivernois pamphlet.
nap-18021207-43: I order Ré, Oléron and Sainte-Marguerite to hold all sentenced deportees. The island prisons receive the condemned.
nap-18021210-44: Deputies, your fatherland is critical. Moderation, prudence, sacrificed passions alone can save it. Switzerland's survival depends on restraint.
nap-18021210-45: I order plans for Quiberon, belle-ile and Boulogne batteries. The coastal defences are planned.
nap-18030203-46: Read the enclosed report. 'Liquidation of newly created pensions' means nothing to me. The pension accounts are opaque.
nap-18030203-47: I have coordinated the convoys from Havre, Dunkerque, Toulon, Genoa, and Corsica so their troops arrive together.
nap-18030204-48: Glad of Fort Dauphin retaken; take directly my full confidence and approval of vigorous measures. Rochambeau earns my trust.
nap-18030205-49: I fifteen thousand men shipped or shipping to saint-domingue. Combine now a 6,500 expedition. The colony receives massive reinforcements.
nap-18030208-50: I order the brisgau commander to receive two Austrian companies. The border garrison accepts the enemy detachment.
nap-18030208-51: My trust in your great talents bids me ask an elementary mathematics work for the national lycees. Haüy, write the textbook for the new schools.
nap-18030209-52: I have received Telemague’s letter thanking me for his appointment as mayor of Cap and affirming his loyalty to the Republic.
nap-18030210-53: Madame de Staël, barred from Paris, has reached Melun. I have ordered the police to send her straight back.
nap-18030501-01: Your letter reached me at the Malmaison. I desire that the conference should not degenerate into a conversation. Show yourself cold, haughty, and even somewhat proud.
nap-18030623-24: I have received your letter, good little Josephine. I perceived with sorrow that you suffered from the journey. But a few days of repose will do much for you. I am very well.
nap-18030701-25: I have received your letter of the of. You do not speak of your health, or of the effect of the baths. I see that you intend to be on your return in eight days. That will afford great pleasure to your Friend, who wearies of being alone.
nap-18030801-02: Irish affairs move me to order secret talks with the United Irish chiefs in Paris. Offer them twenty-five thousand men, forty thousand muskets, guns and powder, and pledge no peace with England till Ireland stands free, if twenty thousand join us on landing.
nap-18030901-03: I return you the despatch from Madrid of the Fructidor. I am surprised that we have no other news. Make out a list of all the complaints we have against Spain, so that we may have materials ready in the event of requiring them.
nap-18031110-04: I return you your despatches, Citizen minister. Tell Citizen Laforest that I have read his despatch with great interest. It will be well to warn the Turkish ambassador that the English, who evidently encourage the Beys, intend to seize upon Egypt.
nap-18031112-05: Citizen general, I have received your letter, and have given orders for hoods to be served out to all the men forming part of the expedition to Ireland, of which you shall have the command. Affairs are settled with Spain and Portugal. Measures have been taken against desertion.
nap-18040101-34: My Friend, I have not received any news from you for several days; I should, however, have been glad to know what effect the waters have had, and how you pass your time. I have been here for the last week, and intend going tomorrow to Boulogne.
nap-18040214-06: For the last week we have been in pursuit of forty brigands composed of Georges and his band, who disembarked at three different places. Another band is to disembark; we have arrested all the men who were to make signals. Savary awaits them at Biville.
nap-18040301-81: You have no doubt heard that Pichegru was arrested yesterday. He was unable to make use of his pistols or of his sabre. He fought with his fists for half an hour with three or four gendarmes. The pleasure experienced by the people of Paris at this arrest does them credit.
nap-18040310-07: I ordered the Duke d’Enghien taken secretly to Vincennes under the name Plessis.
nap-18040410-08: I thank your Holiness for having given a cardinal's hat to the Archbishop of Bologna. I have come to the determination to take into my own hands all that relates to the Concordat with the Italian Republic.
nap-18040510-09: Steube, the minister of Wirtemberg, is a downright fool, as ill-meaning as ignorant. If you can insinuate in a delicate manner that he ought to be recalled, that would please me. Write to General Lannes at Lisbon, and mention the matter to M.
nap-18040530-10: Send Hawkesbury's note to all my agents save Russia, Sweden, Denmark, Porte, with my gloss: gross as its insults run, contempt were my due reply, but England's open maxims overturn Europe's order and must be answered.
nap-18040610-11: This wretched Moreau trial keeps me from the camps. I hope it ends within days. Camp and Paris buzz of a continental war; that would be fatal, turning us from England. Woe to war-seekers! Germany, Austria, Prussia stand with us.
nap-18040712-12: I desire that you will give me by return of post some information on the subject of the family of the Elector of Bavaria, especially concerning His Daughter, and his intentions with regard to that young princess.
nap-18040721-13: Madam and dear Wife, for the last four days since I have been absent from you I have been constantly on horseback, and this exercise has not impaired my health. M. Maret tells me that you intend starting on Monday.
nap-18040803-201: My love, I hope to hear shortly that the waters have done you very much good. I am pained that you have met with so many annoyances. I desire that you should write me often. My health is very good, although I am a little fatigued.
nap-18040806-02: My love, I have been at Calais since midnight. I think of setting out this evening for Dunkirk. I am satisfied with what I see, and am in very good health. I hope that the waters may benefit you, as much as the bustle, the sight of camps, and the ocean have me.
nap-18040901-14: I d'oubril has gone. Although this departure is not good news, still it does not mean a rupture; but it is incalculable what may happen within two or three months. And on the same day Fouche was ordered not to allow any Russians to leave Paris without having paid their debts.
